title: Quenched Bitter Arabian Butter Pudding
description: A lazy-sunday, gooey dessert that marries the richness of butter with the depth of bitter spices, all cooked gently in a bain-marie.
instructions: Place a stainless steel saucepan in a larger pot of simmering water for bain-marie.
Add the butter to the saucepan and melt over low heat, stirring until smooth.
Stir in the cocoa powder, cardamom, black tea leaves, and nettle powder, whisking until fully incorporated.
Pour in the brewed coffee and continue to stir until the mixture thickens to a pourable consistency.
Remove the saucepan from the bain-marie and let it cool for 5 minutes, then stir in a pinch of sea salt.
Grease four ramekins with a small amount of butter, then pour the pudding mixture evenly into each.
Place the filled ramekins in a preheated oven at 160°C and bake for 15 minutes until a thin crust forms.
Remove the ramekins from the oven and allow the puddings to cool to room temperature, then refrigerate for at least 2 hours.
Serve chilled, garnished with crushed pistachios and a light drizzle of lemon juice for brightness.
